approachQuestion.prompt:
A route to print. A directed unweighted graph describes one-way walkways. Given distinct vertices s and t, return a vertex sequence from s to t using the fewest edges, or [] if no route exists. Any minimum-length route is acceptable. Do not return only its length.

Input: read-only outgoing adjacency lists, vertex IDs 0..V-1, 2 <= V <= 200000, 0 <= E <= 400000, no duplicate edges or self-loops.

Example 1: lists=[[1,2],[3],[3],[]], s=0, t=3, output=[0,1,3] or [0,2,3].
Example 2: lists=[[1],[],[]], s=0, t=2, output=[].

options.text: Run BFS from s, marking vertices when enqueued and storing one predecessor per new vertex. If t is reached, follow predecessors from t to s and reverse that sequence.
options.feedback: First discovery in an unweighted BFS supplies a shortest-route predecessor. Following those links reconstructs a real minimum route without copying partial paths during exploration.

options.text: Run BFS, marking vertices when enqueued, but put a complete copied s-to-vertex route into each frontier entry. Return the first route ending at t.
options.feedback: FIFO discovery still produces a minimum route on every input. Copying each partial route adds removable time and storage; one predecessor link per discovered vertex carries the same reconstruction information.

options.text: Use DFS and return the first s-to-t route found, with a visited set.
options.feedback: For lists=[[1,3],[2],[3],[]], s=0,t=3, neighbor order can find [0,1,2,3] first even though [0,3] uses one edge.

options.text: Run BFS and return the discovered vertex IDs in numeric order once t is found.
options.feedback: Discovery membership is not a path. For lists=[[2],[],[1]], s=0,t=1, the valid route is [0,2,1], while numeric order [0,1,2] starts with a nonexistent edge 0->1.

feedback.reason: A traversal must preserve enough edge information to reconstruct a route; the set of reached vertices alone does not identify consecutive steps.
details: Initialize predecessor entries to an unseen sentinel, mark s with a root sentinel, and enqueue s. On each outgoing edge to an unseen vertex, store the current vertex as predecessor and enqueue the neighbor. Stop when t is discovered, or exhaust the queue. If t is unseen, return []. Otherwise append t and its predecessor chain up to s to the result, then reverse the result in place.

The predecessor saved at first BFS discovery belongs to a shortest route. Following predecessors from t yields reversed vertex order, so reverse the returned route once. Unseen t must yield an empty route, not a fabricated predecessor chain.

“Run BFS from s, marking vertices when enqueued and storing one predecessor per new vertex. If t is reached, follow predecessors from t to s and reverse that sequence.”: First discovery in an unweighted BFS supplies a shortest-route predecessor. Following those links reconstructs a real minimum route without copying partial paths during exploration.

“Run BFS, marking vertices when enqueued, but put a complete copied s-to-vertex route into each frontier entry. Return the first route ending at t.”: FIFO discovery still produces a minimum route on every input. Copying each partial route adds removable time and storage; one predecessor link per discovered vertex carries the same reconstruction information.
“Use DFS and return the first s-to-t route found, with a visited set.”: For lists=[[1,3],[2],[3],[]], s=0,t=3, neighbor order can find [0,1,2,3] first even though [0,3] uses one edge.

“Run BFS and return the discovered vertex IDs in numeric order once t is found.”: Discovery membership is not a path. For lists=[[2],[],[1]], s=0,t=1, the valid route is [0,2,1], while numeric order [0,1,2] starts with a nonexistent edge 0->1.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze bfs-parents. V is the total vertex count and E the directed edge count (or undirected edges stored twice where specified). Use preallocated indexed arrays and a V-slot frontier, with constant-time indexing and head/tail queue or stack operations. Include array initialization and all explicitly described scans. No hashing, recursion, array shifting, amortized growth, or input-list copying is used. Exclude the read-only input and returned result; include all other storage. Choose the tightest worst-case pair. The predecessor array also serves as visited state. The returned path holds at most V IDs and is reversed in place with constant extra storage; count its construction time but exclude its storage.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard worst-case bound for the specified implementation.

options.text: O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(V(V + E)) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: BFS plus one route reconstruction uses vertex-sized working arrays and queue.
details: The option “O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space” is tight: initialization costs V, BFS scans each reachable outgoing list once and enqueues each vertex once, and reconstruction/reversal add at most V work. Predecessors and the queue require O(V) auxiliary space even after excluding the returned route. The option “O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space” omits them. The option “O(V(V + E)) time, O(V) auxiliary space” incorrectly repeats traversal per vertex. The option “O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space” charges edge storage although no edges are copied.
